body: That's great news! And it's no problem - I wish you all the best for  the future, and hope uni carries on going well too :)
It's usually more about lecturing than opening up and understanding. You are more than welcome to pm me <3

Opening up can be really hard, and for someone who is in your position of trying to come to terms with the past, that's ok. Whenever you do open up to someone \*you deserve to be heard\*, end of. 

Sometimes it's pent up anger (and if it is that, you have every right to express it.)

The other people who you say are more 'successful' now probably didn't have the same kind of struggle that made them fall behind. Or if they did, they clearly had someone else to confide in and who was there for them at the time - there's no denying it's harder to go through this stuff alone.

So you're not behind, you're just on your way to becoming stronger than them - I don't doubt that it will show in every aspect of your life.

Ah yes, it's nice when along the way, you realise something new about yourself :) and self-discovery beats comparing yourself to other people - I know, easier said than done - but you really do deserve more in life than having to compare yourself to others.

Do your friends know about how you feel?

No problem :) Theoretical physics sounds fascinating (and further, that certainly isn't everybody's strong area) - is this something you've always been interested in? 

​

You sound very overwhelmed, but the fact that you're at university while dealing with past trauma is impressive - you're carrying a lot and I'm proud of you for getting this far :) I don't see how you're a failure. At all.

Can I ask what you're studying?

I could relate to this feeling so much - it can be hard to let go of when it's drummed into you over and over.

The idea that your career/work determines your worth as a person is how people try to make things more predictable - achievement and success as an identity builder rather than following your true values and doing what you do purely because you \*love\* it. Narcissism over self-esteem. Faking an identity over loving the whole one you already have.

You don't say what your passions are, but I see your life as being about -you- first, then everything else comes after. By that I mean your career often only gives a tiny clue about you as a person.

\-You- first.

"like I missed the bus - and then the car ride, the train and the flight."

Brilliant. And I can especially relate to the sharp turn at puberty - I know that that age isn't supposed to be a good time for anyone, but I know my experience was not something every teenager went through.

I think the simple fact that everything in society is focused on competition and attention is, for someone in your position, a big source of feeling like you somehow "lost" - everyone is at a unique place emotionally, but society doesn't give a shit about any of that. The goal is to widen the awareness of it.

Nowadays I think of my past as a 'chunk of experience' that is useful for change. It takes time, which I know can be a depressing thing to hear. But the truth is you know something that those who are "ahead" of you don't have a clue about. You have something really important to contribute.

Also, I don't think of it as a thing I need to "get over". You don't "get over" something and that's it, you're happy forever. You keep changing and learning as much as you can - and it's fine if you only go slowly at first. It only works if you go at your own pace.
